summary: Rabbi Dweck explores the concept of being alone, or badad, as both a state of solitude and a path toward personal and national wholeness. He connects the image of a desolate Jerusalem in Megillat Eicha to the internal human struggle of integrating exiled parts of the self, suggesting that true autonomy requires embracing all aspects of one's being. The class encourages listeners to use moments of stillness to confront these inner parts, mirroring the national process of gathering the Jewish people into a unified whole.
questions: What is the difference between loneliness and solitude?
Why does the Torah describe Israel as a nation that dwells alone?
How can we integrate the parts of ourselves that we feel ashamed of or have exiled?
What is the relationship between our personal inner work and the unity of the Jewish people?
Why do the Hakhamim instruct us to be alone on Tish'a BeAb?
